correctness.rationale: The 14-vertex Fano incidence graph is rebuilt from seven line triples and exactly 21 incidence edges. Two independent face criteria agree on all 8851 faces. The first and second exact Morse matchings each have 4424 ordinary face-covering pairs and critical-cell vector one 0-cell plus one 6-cell. Both completely directed Hasse graphs with 8850 vertices and 52304 covering relations topologically sort, proving acyclicity. Forman gives integral homotopy type S6. All 336 graph automorphisms are counted and checked: 168 GL3(F2) collineations plus 168 polarity swaps, exhaustive by bipartition and noncollinear basis image counting. Exact signed reduced Lefschetz traces for each automorphism are +1. As reduced integral homology is Z only in degree six, their actions on Z are all identity.

evidence: Matsushita–Wakatsuki arXiv:2312.02639v2 Theorem 1.1: Dom(G) Alexander dual = N(complement G). Thus N(complement Heawood) is an exactly equivalent dual problem.

For a cubic four-cycle-free graph H, a disconnected induced four-subset of its complement must comprise one vertex isolated in the complement of the four-set, and all three of its original graph neighbors: the fourteen closed neighborhoods. Hence the ordinary four-cut complex of complement H equals the above dual neighborhood complex in this particular graph.

originality.rationale: Compared exact closed-neighborhood forbidden-subset definition of the Heawood dominance complex, its Alexander-dual description as the neighborhood complex of the dense complement, equivalence with a four-cut condition in that complement, and candidate broader structural theorems. Taylan’s chordal-sphere theorem does not apply to Heawood, and Matsushita–Wakatsuki’s full general-duality/connectivity results do not compute this sphere and orientation character. Indexed Heawood independence/matching/cut/Hom computations are about non-equivalent face conditions. No covering theorem was found, with residual unindexed-priority risk; the full 336-element character is independently derived rather than inferred from a one-dimensional Betti number.
residual_risks: A stronger unpublished or unindexed theorem about dominance complexes of projective-plane incidence graphs might imply this single-graph calculation.
The ordinary four-cut complex of the dense complement is a genuine dual equivalent; an inaccessible preexisting exact result there could imply the homology, even though none was identified.
Some indexed related-result statements were not inspected in full text; they were treated as scope evidence only and not as complete negative checks.
Definitive publication priority and independent scientific validation remain outstanding.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical highly symmetric incidence graph of the smallest projective plane and a natural nonchordal case beyond existing chordal dominance topology. An integral sphere homotopy classification and the full orientation-preserving 336-element symmetry result resolve natural structural questions; neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a routine field-rank recomputation. It also distinguishes homology action from stronger, unproved equivariant homotopy claims.
